One of the best things to build with Argon is a new version of old, boring SaaS.

Old SaaS is legacy software that businesses pay for, but nobody updated it in a long time. 

Thousands of these products charge money. Your version can be better and cost $0.

Here is the whole setup:

1) Find a recurring problem. Look on G2, Capterra, Idea Browser, and Reddit.

2) Read what people complain about in the old product. Put the fixes in yours.

3) Make it focused on one niche. Example: a commercial cleaning company that makes price quotes in a spreadsheet.

4) Give Argon the complaints, the source links, and the workflow. Tell it to explain its plan, build the app, and list what is unfinished. In my test, it made interactive margin calculators with one prompt.

5) Release it as a free tool.

6) Sell your second, third, and fourth tools to the same buyers.

Step 6 only works after step 5. People buy from you after they trust you.

Argon gets the engineering right on the first prompt. For a good design, give it references and work with it.

In the past, I was scared to vibe code a product. The deployment was not good or not secure. 

Frontier AI now makes software that works, and it is probably better than the product it replaces.

Find the complaints, rebuild the product with Argon, then sell the next tool to the same buyers

Since I have the @Dell Pro Max with GB300 on hand and was leaving town for 3 days, I figured I'd give it some real homework to chew on!

I tasked it with an iterative loop of trying to improve my Robotron AI.  The prompt told it to make its "best attempt" at improving the AI, then A/B test it with confidence, then repeat forever.

I came back three days later to find the primary score metric had jumped from 1,000,000 to 5,000,000, a 5X increase in ability!

The GB300 runs 192 copies of MAME, each running an instrumented copy of Robotron.  That's about 8000 frames per second of gameplay.  And it does it all on the GB300's CPU cores, with only half the CPU being used.

Of course, the star of the show is the Blackwell GPU, which handles the reinforcement-learning training.  While I was away, it trained on 2.6 B frames of Robotron gameplay.

Our "old" machine had dual RTX 6000s, so it was no slouch, but the GB300 smokes it!

It's not recursive self-improvement yet, but it's a pretty solid example of iterative self-improvement!

This might be the most underrated AI story of today.

According to CNBC, TikTok's US business is looking to secure multiple gigawatts of computing capacity, with one source suggesting the company is targeting 4 GW by the early 2030s. I don't think people understand how significant this is. We're talking about a social media platform potentially looking to secure enough power and computing infrastructure to rival some of the largest AI data center developments in the country. For perspective, Meta's massive Hyperion data center campus in Louisiana is targeting around 5 GW of capacity.

TikTok already relies primarily on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, and the company has confirmed that $ORCL will remain its primary cloud provider in the United States. On top of that, TikTok is retraining its recommendation algorithm using American user data and is developing AI products focused on large model inference and creative automation. In other words, this isn't necessarily just about supporting people scrolling through videos anymore. TikTok could be preparing for significantly more AI workloads which would require enormous amounts of computing power.

Now connect this to everything else we've been discussing. Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Meta, OpenAI, and xAI are already competing to secure power, GPUs, land, and data center capacity. Now we're seeing another major technology platform potentially entering that same competition at the gigawatt scale. And remember, these companies cannot simply decide they want another gigawatt of computing capacity and have it available tomorrow. They need electricity, substations, cooling infrastructure, networking equipment, GPUs, memory, and facilities capable of supporting all of it.

This is exactly why I remain so bullish on the companies supplying the infrastructure behind AI. Whether we're talking about $NVDA, $MU, $ORCL, $BE, or the broader networking and power ecosystem, the number of potential customers competing for limited resources continues to grow. What's particularly interesting is that this demand is increasingly coming from companies outside the handful of frontier AI labs everyone focuses on. I think we're still underestimating just how much infrastructure the AI economy is going to need over the next decade.

Gemini 4 Carbon Checkpoint: Leaks, Sightings and New context.

Since my previous post about the Gemini 4 Carbon discovery, more reported details and community sightings have surfaced. Here’s an updated overview of what’s been circulating, alongside my own interpretation.

TL;DR: Carbon is reportedly Google’s internal experimental branch being developed alongside the Argon checkpoint, with a strong focus on complex coding, long-running tasks, and agentic workflows.

What’s new about this unreleased internal model:

Internal evaluations reportedly show substantial gains on SWE-bench and Deep SWE compared with earlier Barium-B checkpoints. One employee described it as feeling like “Opus 5.5,” while some employees had acknowledged that Gemini Argon still fell short in certain areas.

Reports suggest that internal A/B testing has expanded across testing environments, primarily AGY, though other environments may also be involved.

Carbon’s eventual release format remains unclear. It could replace Argon directly, become a separate performance tier within the Gemini 4 lineup, or serve as a final refinement of Argon that addresses its remaining weaknesses - including concerns from users who consider it “benchmaxxed.”

Carbon appears to belong to Gemini 4’s ongoing checkpoint development process, which uses element-based names such as Argon, Barium, and Carbon. Internal documents identified Barium-B as the build chosen for Argon’s public release. That leaves open the possibility that Carbon could become an upgraded checkpoint within Gemini 4.x, potentially serving as a polished, stable final version of Gemini 4 Argon. That’s my interpretation, though, rather than a confirmed plan.

Some community members expect Gemini 4 Flash to launch soon, possibly alongside Carbon. There have been hints of a Flash release, but, from what I’ve seen, there isn’t enough evidence to establish either that timing or a connection to Carbon.

Carbon reportedly runs two to four times slower than Argon, which could suggest a heavier reasoning model. The latest checkpoint attracted attention a few days ago after apparently strong demonstrations in Arena. Accounts describe the preceding checkpoint as poor, making the latest version’s reported jump in capability especially striking.

Perhaps the most notable development: community members report encountering Carbon in LMSYS Arena. If those sightings are accurate, Google may be following a testing approach similar to Argon’s, where a lucky prompt could give someone a chance to interact with the unreleased model.

My personal take is that Google may be positioning Carbon to compete for the top spot ahead of Fable 5.5. Another possibility is that a backup checkpoint developed into a much stronger candidate than expected following Argon’s release and successive improvements.

If those reported gains hold up, Carbon could address several weaknesses in Google’s current flagship, Gemini 4 Argon: greater reliability, stronger performance on long-running tasks involving multiple steps, and improvements in important benchmark areas where Argon trails. It might also deliver more cost-efficient task completion, although that remains speculative.

What do you think? will Carbon appear first as an experimental model in AI Studio, or arrive through another phased rollout? If you’ve encountered it or experimented with it and feel comfortable sharing, drop your observations below.

During this red-teaming exercise, we also found a vulnerability that allows for unauthenticated remote code execution in Brotli, a widely-deployed compression library included in many pieces of software such as Node.js, Bun, and Envoy.

The flaw could let an attacker run their own code on affected systems by sending or replying with malicious compressed data, without any need to create a user account. That is, an unpatched server that accepts compressed input could be taken over by a malicious client, and an unpatched client that accepts compressed input (such as “curl --compressed”) could be taken over by a malicious server.

This root cause issue was actually fixed in the Brotli source code in February, but it wasn’t known at the time that it gave rise to a security vulnerability and there was no more recent release of Brotli. Since Brotli is built into other software, any software which includes this library needs to take the update too, followed by the users of that software. We disclosed the vulnerability to Brotli and other downstream projects such as Node.js, which released or are currently releasing security updates, and Brotli cut new release versions and published a CVE.

2026.10.24【周末论市：警惕有个坑】
        10月19日至23日，A股走出了先撑后跌、周五强势反弹的一周。周一沪指上涨0.39%，深成指上涨0.13%，创业板指却下跌0.94%，市场分化已经显露；随后几个交易日，科技成长板块持续承压，市场调整不断加深。到了周五，行情突然逆转，三大指数低开高走，沪指上涨0.89%，深成指上涨2.79%，创业板指大涨4.16%，两市成交额放大至约1.96万亿元，全市场超过4500只个股上涨。市场要见底了吗？
         这一周最重要的特征，不是周五涨了多少，而是市场在经历连续下跌后，终于出现了一次力度很强的反弹。但我要强调，单日大涨不等于趋势反转，周五的反弹也不能抹去此前市场暴露出来的风险。按周度数据看，沪指全周下跌0.69%，深成指下跌1.09%，创业板指下跌3.18%。这说明市场整体仍然承压，尤其是创业板代表的成长方向，弱势并没有因为周五一根大阳线就被彻底扭转。最重要的一点，看涨幅榜是超跌的科技故事会带动，低估值纹丝不动，这明显不是反转！
          回顾本周的市场表现，我此前反复强调的几个问题，已经越来越清楚。第一，科技概念的风险仍然是市场不能回避的问题。前期被资金反复炒作的算力硬件、人工智能相关概念，在调整中暴露出明显的脆弱性。10月22日，创业板指单日下跌4.37%，新易盛跌超12%，多只科技概念股大幅下挫。到了23日，科技成长板块又成为反弹的重要力量。这恰恰说明，当前资金博弈激烈，热点反转速度很快。对于缺乏业绩支撑、估值过高的概念股，我依然不认为一次暴涨就能证明风险解除。真正值得关注的，是企业有没有核心技术、真实订单和持续盈利能力，而不是股价能不能连续涨停。
        第二，低估值股票的价值修复依然值得期待，但不能把个别银行股创新高直接等同于市场全面走强。本周工商银行、建设银行再创历史新高，银行板块局部回暖，说明低估值方向仍有资金关注。然而，银行股的上涨究竟是价值修复，还是机构在关键时刻稳定指数，仍然需要后续走势来验证。我的观点一直很明确：低估值股票长期被忽视，价值修复不可能一日完成；但如果市场只有少数权重股支撑指数，大量个股却持续下跌，这样的行情就谈不上真正健康。
         第三，610天线已经成为下一阶段最重要的观察位置。本周沪指在下跌过程中触及610天线，随后出现回升。我一直重视这条长期均线，因为它是判断市场中长期趋势的重要参考。周五的强势反弹，给市场带来了一定喘息空间，但现在就宣布610天线已经确认见底，显然还为时过早。尤其科创50距离610还很远，而科创板估值最高，是必然打到610的！
         对于周五的反弹，我的判断是：这是一次有力度的反弹，但还构不成反转。真正决定后市方向的，不是某一天涨得有多猛，而是反弹能否延续，市场广度能否保持，如果继续靠科技故事会拉抬，那就是镰刀割多少韭菜的问题，市场必然再次回落。尤其周五美股下跌，如果下周A股反弹迅速衰减，并且持续走弱，那么周五的上涨就可能只是调整过程中的一次强力反抽。
           展望下周，我重点观察三个信号：一是沪指在610天线附近能否保持稳定，二是周五的放量上涨能否延续，三是上涨能否从少数热点扩散到更广泛的个股。如果这三个信号不能得到后续走势的支持，我仍然不会轻易认定市场已经反转。尤其是前期涨幅巨大、估值高企的科技概念，即使继续反弹，也不值得不加区分地追涨。
         从板块来说，未来一旦有行情，哪个板块机会最大？我觉得医药股里肯定会出大牛股，包括疫苗类，如果是动物疫苗还有宠物概念，潜力很大，电力股是长期看好的重头戏，毕竟有算电协同，算力估值太高我们不建议做，电力可以，再其次就是看战略小金属里有没有低估值品种，这个也有想象空间，但整体看这都是后话，首要任务要确定这后面是不是一个坑，别偷鸡不成蚀把米！
        本周市场给出的教训很清楚：下跌时不能盲目抄底，反弹时同样不能盲目追高。610天线的考验还没有结束，周五的反弹究竟是趋势转折的开始，还是下跌过程中的一次强力反抽，需要下周行情给出答案。在信号真正明朗之前，我宁愿建议耐心等待，也不会建议为了交易而交易。况且你们了解到的只是官方公布的好消息，经济走势的暗面你们一无所知，那里又黑又冷。。。。

《为什么中国的银行能走出独立于西方银行的行情？》

中国与海外看似都在政府加杠杆、财政扩张，为什么中国银行表现反而不错？答案不在景气度的高低，而在周期位置与政策投向的差异。日本的对照很能说明问题：日本银行同样面临浮亏问题，但其利率上升处于偏早期，浮亏对盈利仍是贡献，而欧美一些银行已处于周期中后期，这就是周期位置的不同。

具体到中国银行业，可以从三个角度理解：

第一，财政投向不同。 欧美市场一看到财政扩张、赤字加码，直接反应是通胀上升并抛售长期债券。中国的财政投向则更加多元：今年年初两会提出的13.9万亿元政府总融资计划中，约3万亿元与金融稳定相关，包括地方政府债务置换，也包括对金融机构3000亿元的注资。这些政策对金融机构资产负债表起到修复作用——也就是说，今年新增的13.9万亿元融资中约1/5是在做金融稳定，对银行的影响自然不同。

第二，利率周期不同。 欧美处于高利率环境的时间比中国更长，高利率可能带来信用成本、存款成本上升、债券浮亏等一系列问题。中国利率周期处于历史较低位置，且总体稳定、波动不大。一个关键数字是：据测算，最近几年银行其他非息收入对利润的贡献每年在1—2个百分点左右，其中相当一部分正是债券投资收益和债券浮盈兑现。同样的债券，在欧美利率环境下是拖累，在中国利率环境下却是利润贡献。

第三，信用周期不同。 衡量信用周期可用"信贷脉冲"这一指标，即以新增信贷或社融除以GDP，用以刻画金融周期位置。结论是：中国金融周期处于最近几年比较低的位置，而海外金融周期处于过去几年偏高的位置，信贷脉冲仍处扩张阶段。不良率同样反映信用周期位置——中国不良率约1.5%，处于历史偏低位置且非常稳定，今年整体基本持平；而海外利率环境较高，不良率可能逐渐上升，不确定性高于中国。

最后总结：

"东升西降"的实质并不是东方银行比西方银行更赚钱，而是同一个高利率环境在不同周期位置上产生了相反的效果：欧美银行已从高利率周期上半段进入中后段，息差扩张空间收窄、信用成本与存款成本开始上行、账面债券浮亏积累，而长端利率上行的背后还叠加了财政可持续性的长期担忧；中国银行则处于利率周期的低位、信用周期的低位，财政扩张中又有相当比例直接用于修复金融机构资产负债表，债券在资产端反而是利润来源。

因此，这一分化首先反映的是市场担忧点的转移：从"高利率利好银行盈利"，转向"高利率本身会成为风险来源"。它不代表长期的趋势性拐点，也不意味着海外银行即将集中爆雷；真正需要持续跟踪的，是利率将继续上行、在通胀高位长期停留，还是能够较快回落——因为高利率环境下，哪个环节会先出问题，往往只有在问题发生之后才能确认。

这也是我反复跟星球朋友说的，不要尝试预测系统性的流动性冲击，我们根本不知道在高利率环境下，哪个机构、行业、板块先爆雷。

Five Errors Per Million. A New Record.

Quantinuum just reported a logical error rate of 5 per million operations on its Helios machine.

That is 99.9995% logical fidelity, ten times better than its own record from September.

Before anyone panics: this does not break any encryption. It is a benchmark for reliable computation, not an attack. Quantinuum says it points toward Apollo, a fault-tolerant machine it is targeting for 2029.

Why it still matters. Long quantum attacks need reliable logical qubits, and error correction is the gap between today's noisy machines and ones that can run them. Earlier this year Google researchers estimated that fewer than 500,000 physical qubits could derive a private key from an exposed public key in about nine minutes.

Every result like this moves the date a little closer, and nobody knows which one is the last.

QuanChain does not bet on a date. Its oracle tracks the cost per logical qubit-hour, and wallets move to stronger security levels at their next spend. Value at rest sits behind an address hash, not an exposed public key.

The hardware is getting better. The design should not need a forecast.

Expert Takeaways: TSMC

1. CoWoS Capacity, Fab Breakdown, Spill‑Over Orders & Customer Allocation

Capacity Expansion: TSMC's internal CoWoS monthly capacity is targeted to reach 130k wafers by end-2026, with a long-term goal of 260k wafers/month by 2028 (excluding OSAT volumes).

Demand Growth: Market demand for CoWoS has increased by at least 26% compared to early-2026 levels.

Fab Breakdown: AP8 full capacity is 50k wafers (>40k expected by end-2026); AP7-P1 reached its 35k full-load target after ramping in August; AP7-P2 focuses primarily on SoIC; US AP1 will not ramp significantly by year-end; legacy AP1–AP6 fabs handle the remaining volume.

Expansion Bottlenecks: New packaging fab construction takes about three years from groundbreaking to bottleneck-limited full output, constrained mainly by hybrid bonding and 3–4 nm-grade CMP flatness requirements.

OSAT Spill-Over Strategy: Lower-margin orders are routed to external OSATs (ASE, SPIL, Amkor) under signed LTAs, reserving TSMC’s internal capacity for high-value customers.

Customer Allocation Split: Nvidia (60%), Broadcom (15%), AMD (10%), Marvell (6%), AWS in-house silicon (5%), MediaTek (2%), and others (3%).

2. SoIC Capacity Roadmap, Capital Intensity, Fab Bottlenecks & End‑Use Drivers

Capacity Roadmap: Targeted at 15k wafers/month by end-2026, 24–28k by end-2027, and up to 45k by end-2028 (~90% CAGR in 2027).

Capital Intensity & Bottlenecks: Capital intensity is $6.8–7.0 billion per 10k monthly wafers. Hybrid-bonding pick-and-place tools are the initial bottleneck, shifting dynamically to PVD and PECVD.

Manufacturing Limits: High CMP flatness and particle cleanliness requirements create a hardware ceiling below CoWoS scale. Capacity is concentrated at Chiayi AP7 through end-2027 (long-term potential 40–50k/month). US AP1 will take future volume but faces a long learning curve requiring Taiwan team transfer.

Key Demand Drivers: Nvidia (Rubin Ultra / Feynman), AMD (MI400 / Venice), Apple (M5 Pro / Max), and Broadcom ASICs slated for 2027.

3. Competitive Landscape (Intel / Samsung), Yields & Risk Mitigation

Intel EMIB-T Status: Yield estimates vary from ~90% (supply chain) to 38–40% (test-vehicle data). EMIB-T die cost is ~50% of CoWoS-L. Intel outsources all backend assembly to Amkor across Longtan, Portugal, and Arizona.

Samsung & Competitor Scale: Samsung I-Cube yield maturity lags peers, with meaningful competitive threats unlikely until post-2030 when hybrid bonding matures. Overall, TSMC’s advanced packaging volume is ~5× that of Intel.

Customer De-Risking: Google is validating EMIB-T as a backup due to TSMC tightness, costs, and US policy. Broadcom is evaluating EMIB-T and Samsung capacity, while building a joint substrate/FC-BGA facility in Singapore with Toppan.

4. CoPoS Technical Bottlenecks, Production Timeline & Silicon Utilization

Realistic Timeline: Mass CoPoS production in 2027–2028 is overly optimistic. AP7 has started qualification, aiming for limited NPI in 2027, low-volume production (LVM) for Nvidia Feynman in H2-2028, and true high-volume manufacturing (HVM) in 2029–2030. Glass-core TGV technology is deferred to post-2030.

Technical Challenges: Five core bottlenecks include substrate warpage, fine-pitch RDL lithography, coat-and-plate uniformity, ~70% copper-fill yield for TGV vias, and large-format panel-tool standardization.

Fab Footprint & Wafer Efficiency: US AP2 is provisionally planned for CoPoS. CoPoS requires greenfield fabs and won't cannibalize CoWoS. For large die sizes (e.g., 75×75 mm), CoPoS panel utilization reaches >84%, compared to just 48% on 12-inch circular wafers.

5. TSMC Co-Development Model & CPO Technology Outlook

Deep Joint Development: Advanced packaging is not off-the-shelf; TSMC collaborates closely with key customers on architecture, process flow, equipment limits, photomasks, and probe cards (e.g., scaling SpaceX probe sites from 4–6 up to 32up).

CPO Reality: Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) is not inherently tied to glass and can be built on silicon stacks. Key factors for success are I/O alignment precision and yield parity with CoWoS. Glass-based CPO currently faces high warpage and fracture risks.

6. Capital Expenditure, HPC Exposure & OSAT Dynamics

CapEx Upside: TSMC total capex guidance was revised up from $52–56B to $60–64B, with ~10% allocated to backend packaging (CoWoS/SooS).

Revenue Exposure: High Performance Computing (HPC) accounted for 68% of TSMC's Q3 revenue.

OSAT Role: External OSAT capacity serves purely as supplementary volume and cannot replace TSMC’s core leadership in high-end advanced packaging.

7. New-Fab Constraints, Capacity Methodology & Portfolio Strategy

Capacity Definition: Advanced-packaging fab capacity is defined by dynamic bottleneck tool stations (lithography, develop, die-bond, hybrid-bond) rather than physical floor space, creating variable output profiles across fabs.

A9/A10 & Future Fabs: Insider visibility on A9/A10 schedules remains limited with no firm dates.

Strategy: TSMC routes low-margin work externally while shifting internal capital toward next-gen CoPoS. Hybrid bonding and CMP flatness will remain recurring bottlenecks as Nvidia Feynman and HBM4-E ramp.

8. Supply-Chain Frictions from Constrained CoWoS-S Capacity

CoWoS-S Shortages: Shifted focus toward CoWoS-L has left CoWoS-S expansion constrained, weighing on 2026 customer deliveries.

Impacted Programs: TPU v7 / v8t implementations relying on CoWoS-S continue to face supply headwinds.

Alternative Approaches: Broadcom’s Sunfish uses CoWoS-L and is positioned well for 2027. Broadcom v8t and Humu-fish evaluated EMIB-T as an alternative, but yields remain inadequate, keeping supply pressure high on CoWoS-S programs.

The world is getting more of its electricity from renewables but less from nuclear power.

If the world is to reduce its carbon emissions and tackle climate change, it needs to move away from fossil fuels to low-carbon power.

There are two key sources of low-carbon electricity: renewables — which include solar, wind, hydropower and others — and nuclear power.

While rapid growth in solar and wind has increased the amount of electricity coming from renewables, a lack of enthusiasm for nuclear means it’s playing a shrinking role in the global mix.

In the chart, you can see the share of global electricity coming from fossil fuels, renewables, and nuclear since 1985. Since 2000, nuclear and renewables have followed very different trajectories. Back then, both accounted for a similar share of global electricity. But in 2025, renewables made up more than three times as much: 34% compared to 9%.

The total amount of electricity produced by nuclear plants is about the same as it was two decades ago. But because the world produces much more electricity overall, its share of the electricity mix has declined.

(written by @_HannahRitchie and @parriagadap)

I visited Wurster Hall at UC Berkeley today. It was designed by, and currently houses, the architecture faculty.

The UC Berkeley website notes that "Wurster is often voted Berkeley's ugliest building."

I visited because I was curious about whether it would in person seem as unattractive as it does in photos. And, in short: it does. It's gaunt, austere, and filmed in grime. On an elysian campus, it stands out for its bleak hostility. It reminds me of the German submarine base in Bordeaux.

The UC Berkeley page agrees that it was never designed to be attractive, quoting the curator of their design archives: “Wurster and his handpicked architects didn’t want anything romantic, or sentimental — they hated the idea of ‘making pretty buildings. They wanted a serious building.”

I guess we have to concede success relative to their stated goals, but it does make one wonder what it all says about architecture as a discipline.

There is an absolute barrage of inference providers popping up that get to $1M/mo extremely quickly.

This is the rough economics of inference providers:

Even if you rent on-demand B300s at $8/GPU-hr, many open source models (GLM 5.3, Kimi K3, DeepSeek 4.1 Flash / Pro) can get you >$10-20/GPU-hr at reasonable throughputs (100tok/s). DeepInfer from DeepSeek directly shows they can get $38/GPU-hr on off-peak hours. Every chip / model has a different throughput / interactivity curve, but there is a lot of arbitrage between even high rental spot prices and token prices. New chips (Vera Rubins) also change this meaningfully. Your ability to be making gross margin relies on your utilization and how good your stack is.

Gateways like OpenRouter, Vercel and more help solve that problem by aggregating demand to you. May inference providers discount their tokens to get longer term commits too. I've even heard stories of selling back Chinese model tokens to Chinese labs!

One thorn in the economics of these players is that many Chinese open source model labs are now asking for rev share if you're at a certain scale, espp for pre-release access to their models for day 1 support. That further pushes the threshold to be in the money.

The barrier to entry seems low and falling. There are even stories of smaller ones who can "vibe code" a way to stand up OSS models on a cluster they rent. And as a result, we're seeing 10s of such companies pop up almost every week and immediately skyrocketing revenue at low-ish gross margin and raising rounds on the back of that.

Unsurprisingly, because the actual service provided seems commodity, this eventually drives up compute prices and drives down token prices. In theory, it would seem like neoclouds who have the lowest cost of compute and themselves have started inference businesses would win the race to the bottom (Crusoe Coreweave Nebius and GMI all have inference businesses), with larger players (Modal Fireworks Baseten) being second because they are well capitalized to make bigger compute commits cheaply and have demand (high utilization), but the reality is the pie is growing so quickly that even upstarts are absolutely crushing it and growing aggressively (inference dot net, DeepInfra, Wafer, Relace, Morph).

Strategies vary across the board: neoclouds want to serve inference, inference players want to be neoclouds and do higher margin reserved instances / post training, and some want to go heterogeneous hardware or creatively flexible compute constructs.

The risks are: do open source models continue to be competitive? Will their creators rent seek more? Will their shape change compute needs? How do different chips change economics? Who gets compute in a supply crunch?

For now, there are many inference providers and they’re all ripping!

Good morning @quipnetwork ☕️

I want to cover the quantum research result that I think is the single most important experimental finding for understanding the urgency of post-quantum security.

The 2023 IBM quantum error correction paper in Nature.

Not the Willow chip. Not the qubit count records. This specific paper. Here's why it changed how I think about the timeline.

The paper demonstrated a repetition code running on 127 physical qubits where the logical error rate decreased as the code distance increased.

That sentence requires unpacking because the implication is enormous.

Previous quantum error correction implementations shared a fundamental problem: as you added more qubits to improve error correction the overhead introduced new errors at roughly the same rate as the correction removed them. The net improvement was marginal. The scaling relationship was unfavorable.

The IBM Nature paper showed the relationship inverting.

More qubits. Better error correction. Net logical error rate going down as code distance goes up.

For the first time experimentally the error correction was winning against the noise.

Google's Willow result confirmed this a year later at larger scale and higher code distance. Two independent research groups. Two different hardware architectures. Same conclusion.

Quantum error correction scales favorably.

Here is the research implication stated as precisely as I can:

The engineering barrier that made fault-tolerant quantum computation seem perpetually 10 years away was the unfavorable scaling of error correction overhead. Every experimental result before 2023 suggested that noise grew faster than correction could compensate.

2023 and 2025 showed experimentally that this scaling relationship flips at sufficient code distance.

The barrier was real. Now it's been crossed. The path to fault-tolerant computation is open in a way it demonstrably was not before.

Shor's algorithm runs on fault-tolerant quantum hardware. The discrete logarithm problem the mathematical foundation of every wallet signature in crypto breaks on fault-tolerant quantum hardware.

The experimental confirmation that fault-tolerant scaling works changes the timeline from "theoretically possible but practically uncertain" to "engineering execution problem on a known trajectory."

Those are not the same thing.

My honest long view:

I read a lot of quantum research. Most results are incremental. Some are significant. A few are genuinely pivotal.

The favorable error correction scaling results from IBM and Google are pivotal. They are the experimental confirmation that the theoretical path to cryptographically relevant quantum computation is physically real rather than mathematically assumed.

Everything downstream of that confirmation @quipnetwork 's post-quantum wallets, the compute marketplace, the PoUW mechanism, the urgency of the airdrop window at https://t.co/5aKccd0qVp makes more sense when you understand what those papers actually proved.

The researchers updated their models in 2023. Most of CT hasn't updated theirs yet.

🚨 Et si le krach de la mémoire attendu en 2028 n’arrivait jamais ?

70–80 % de la surface de silicium d’un rack IA est de la mémoire. La HBM consomme 3 à 4 fois plus de wafers par Go que la DDR5.

Certaines actions mémoire cotent à 2x leurs leurs PE. Bernstein et SA en parle : 

Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis) et Stacy Rasgon (Bernstein) viennent de partager leurs perspectives sur l'industrie des semi-conducteurs au CASPA CEO Summit.

Plusieurs déclarations importantes pour les investisseurs.

1️⃣ Les véritables goulots :

Dylan Patel classe les contraintes industrielles dans cet ordre :

1/Substrats avancés, PCB et matériaux.
2/Mémoire HBM et DRAM.
3/Lasers et composants optiques.
4/Équipements et capacités de fabrication.
5/Électricité et infrastructures.

Il estime que près de 50 GW de data centers seront en construction dans le monde en 2027.

Mais fabriquer suffisamment de substrats avancés pourrait être beaucoup plus difficile que trouver de nouvelles solutions d'alimentation électrique.

🇹🇼 Unimicron (3037), Kinsus (3189) et Nan Ya PCB (8046) sont particulièrement bien positionnés sur ce marché.

2️⃣ Le supercycle de la mémoire pourrait durer bien plus longtemps que prévu.

Stacy souligne un paradoxe :

Certains fabricants de mémoire se négocient entre 2 et 4 fois leurs bénéfices prévisionnels.

La HBM nécessite environ 3 à 4 fois plus de wafers que la DDR5 conventionnelle pour produire une quantité équivalente de mémoire.

Les nouvelles salles blanches ne permettront d'augmenter significativement les capacités qu'en 2028-2029.

Le marché anticipe déjà un effondrement des prix de la DRAM en 2028.

Sa question : « Et si cela ne se produisait pas ? »

🇰🇷 SK hynix, Samsung et 🇺🇸 Micron pourraient maintenir des bénéfices exceptionnellement élevés plus longtemps qu'anticipé.

3️⃣ NVIDIA commence à perdre des parts de marché face aux ASIC.

Selon Dylan, NVIDIA consomme déjà une proportion décroissante des capacités mondiales de HBM et de CoWoS.

Google, Amazon et AMD gagnent du terrain.

Mais attention : NVIDIA pourrait continuer à doubler ses bénéfices malgré cette baisse de part relative.

4️⃣ Le véritable enjeu sera la répartition des marges.

Dylan estime que le coût d'un GW d'infrastructure IA est passé d'environ 40 Md$ en 2024 à plus de 60 Md$ en 2026.

Une part considérable de cette valeur est captée par NVIDIA et les autres concepteurs de puces.

Si les hyperscalers internalisent davantage leur conception, une partie des profits pourrait se déplacer vers les fournisseurs de mémoire, de substrats et de composants industriels.

🇹🇼 Pour les investisseurs taïwanais, cela renforce l'intérêt de TSMC, Unimicron, Kinsus et Nan Ya PCB.

Le marché IA peut continuer à exploser sans que NVIDIA conserve indéfiniment la même part de la valeur.

📅 2027-2028 : pénuries 
2029 : première véritable interrogation sur le risque de surcapacités.

四家云厂商二季度一共花掉1651亿美元买设备、建机房，比一年前多出87%。

$SOXX却在10月22日一天跌了6.79%。

钱还在往产业链里砸，股价先跌了一大段。要看懂这种背离，得先把这笔钱流去了哪里画清楚。

二季度的现金资本开支：$AMZN 542亿美元，$GOOGL 449亿，$MSFT 358亿，$META 301亿。

Meta已经先交了三季度：资本开支（含融资租赁本金）349.1亿美元，经营现金流327.9亿，自由现金流变成负21.2亿。全年指引收窄到1350亿至1450亿美元。

赚来的现金，已经不够付这一季的建设账单。

这笔钱的流向，可以压成一条链：

云厂商 → 服务器整机 → GPU/ASIC → 代工、先进封装、HBM → 设备、EDA

链条旁边还有三条支线：网络交换、光模块、电力散热。

主链决定算力造不造得出来，支线决定造出来的算力能不能连起来、跑起来。

第一站是服务器整机。

鸿海、广达、$DELL、$SMCI 把GPU、内存、网卡和电源装进机柜。鸿海三季度营收3.03万亿新台币，环比增长20.44%。

这一环收入大、毛利薄，钱从这里过一手，大部分继续往上游走。

第二站是计算芯片，相当于数据中心的大脑。

$NVDA 截至7月的季度数据中心收入890亿美元，同比增长117%，其中直接来自超大规模云厂商的有487亿。

它卡住的是CUDA软件生态和整机柜系统。客户想换掉它，要重写软件、重新验证集群。

替代路线是定制ASIC。$AVGO 同期AI半导体收入167亿美元，同比增长221%，定制加速器占其中73%，客户包括谷歌TPU、OpenAI和Meta。$MRVL 走的是同一条路。

云厂商自己设计芯片，是为了压低每一次推理的成本，这部分钱会从GPU分流出去一块。

第三站是制造。

$TSM 三季度营收467.2亿美元，7纳米及以下先进制程占晶圆收入79%。不管GPU还是ASIC，最先进的那几代大多要回到台积电下单。

芯片造好以后还要做CoWoS先进封装，把计算芯片和HBM拼在同一块中介层上。这道工序过去两年一直是AI芯片出货的瓶颈之一，日月光和 $AMKR 在后段分担部分产能。

HBM是贴在计算芯片旁边的高速记忆。

计算再快，数据喂不进来也只能空转。

$MU 截至9月3日的季度营收542.3亿美元，一年前同期只有113.2亿。SK海力士二季度营业利润率达到76%。

亚马逊把2026年资本开支上调到约2200亿美元时，给出的原因是存储涨价。

云厂商多花的钱里，有一部分直接变成了存储厂的利润。

第四站是更上游的设备和设计工具。

$ASML 三季度收入116.6亿欧元，系统销售里逻辑占54%、存储占46%。公司说2027和2028年按现有计划的供给都无法完全满足需求，部分客户已经想下2029、2030年的订单。

$AMAT、$LRCX、$KLAC 分别守着沉积、刻蚀和检测量测。

$CDNS、$SNPS 的EDA软件和 $ARM 的架构授权，在芯片流片之前就先收钱。

三条支线同样在分钱。

网络交换把几万张卡连成一台机器。$ANET 做以太网交换机，$AVGO 三季度AI网络收入是一年前的2.5倍以上，$NVDA 自己也卖交换机，Spectrum-6已经支持共封装光学。

光模块把电信号转成光信号跑长距离，相当于机房里的神经。$LITE、$COHR 供应激光器和模块，$CRDO 做有源电缆和高速互联芯片，中际旭创是800G、1.6T光模块的主要供应商之一。

电力散热决定机房能不能通上电、会不会过热。$VRT 给出的三季度收入指引是36.5亿至38.5亿美元，有机增长34%至36%；$GEV、$ETN、$BE 分别对应发电设备、配电和现场供电。

正如9/25那条写的："公司可以讲故事，产业链很难一起配合演。"

这张地图的用处就在这里。云厂商资本开支一上调，台积电、海力士、ASML的数字应该跟着动；哪一环先停下来，往往比云厂商自己改口来得更早。

接下来几天的时间表：

美东10月27日晚8点（北京10月28日早8点），SK海力士三季度电话会。

美东10月28日盘前，$VRT 发布三季度业绩，11点电话会（北京23点）。

同一天下午2点（北京10月29日凌晨2点），美联储公布利率决议。

美东10月28日盘后，$GOOGL 下午4点半、$MSFT 下午5点半开电话会（北京10月29日凌晨4点半、5点半）。

美东10月29日下午5点（北京10月30日早5点），$AMZN 电话会。

要看三件事：全年和2027年资本开支有没有继续上调，云收入增速能不能盖住折旧，自由现金流还要被压多久。

这个系列会沿着这张图一环一环拆：GPU、定制ASIC、台积电代工、半导体设备、EDA与IP、存储与HBM、先进封装、服务器CPU、网络交换、光模块、服务器整机、电力散热，再回到云厂商的资本开支。

钱流得最快的环节，往往也是股价最先把预期打满的环节。

7. Or could we do much better by more critically assessing all our strategic options and comparing them to the Ministry's? 

8. My argument on the show was that I am not convinced about GhanaChat offering the best value for our money. 

9. It would take many pages to explain my position fully. But in this post I will highlight just the most important points.

10. Attached are extracts from page 13, 50, and 68 of Ghana's AI strategy.

11. If you have even the barest exposure to AI, you can see a massive error. Can you?

12. The target for how much computing capacity the country needs for next year (2027) is indicated as "1021 FLOPS" and the 2035 target as "1025 FLOPS".

13. If this was indeed correct, it would mean that the Ministry would like the entire computing capacity of the country in 2027 to be equivalent to a 1970s desktop computer. Or 2% of the capacity of the 1980 Intel math chip.

14. Howzat?

15. I'm sure you can agree that this would be totally ridiculous if that was the Ministry's intent. So, what happened?

16. Somebody who didn't fully understand how FLOPS work must have been involved in the drafting. What was meant to be 10 raised to the power 21 operations per second (10²¹ operations a second) was written out as "1021". Same for "1025". 

17. Why wasn't the error caught? Because in Ghana when doing "consultations", governments rarely engage independent and critical voices who will point out absurdities without fear of offending big men and women.

18. I am not being petty. There is a serious strategic confusion beyond mere typos.

19. Read properly as 10²¹ FLOPS, the Ministry is telling us that by next year it will have some 200,000 of Nvidia's newest chips in use in Ghana, 500 MW of power devoted to AI, all costing about US$24 billion (close to the Ghanaian government's entire programmed spending for 2026). 

20. The US$250 million AI datacenter now being procured supplies about 1% of this 2027 target.

21. Howzat?

22. Clearly, no serious critique of the plan would have okayed such a vision. Throughout the ministry's own review, cabinet approval, and a high-profile media launch, it is absolutely clear that not one critical reviewer was engaged.

23. My first major point here is that this is classic KATANOMICS: the lack of critical policy audiences. This is exactly how a sugar factory that was "designed from the start to fail" was allowed to be built. Many programs and initiatives in Ghana fail for precisely this absence of critical review.

24. In the strategy, you find statements like: "government aggressively building AI compute clusters" and by courting hyperscalers, "to leverage the scaling laws towards building general purpose AI and AGI". Then: "drastically increase Ghana's energy capacity 0.5 to 1 OOM per year". "OOM" means "order of magnitude".

25. When I challenged the Minister on TV, he confidently rebutted by claiming that the Energy Minister/Ministry has assured him of feasibility. Ghana's energy Ministry is committing to increase Ghana's power output by 3x to 10x EVERY YEAR so that the Digital Minister can deliver his AI strategy? Did anyone in Cabinet not protest that this projection in 8 years would mean expanding Ghana's electricity output by 10,000x?

26. I can bet you any amount that the Energy Minister will deny making any such commitments in Cabinet. Can we have clarity? Can JoyNews check?

27.  Page 68 of the strategy defines an "Artificial General Intelligence Lab" as "an AI lab with access to more than 1010 compute". No unit is given at all. In fact, as written it is totally meaningless. What they likely mean is that Ghana will support the establishment of a lab with computing capacity of 10¹⁰ FLOPS (10 gigaFLOPS).

28. The problem is that such a lab would be totally useless. To give you perspective, an iPhone 7 has about 350 gigaFLOPS of capacity.

29. What would be required to meet the Ministry's 2027 AI target? If for frontier model development, then the following spec would be reasonable: 400,000 16-bit Nvidia B300 GPU units, 1,114 MW of dedicated power (which is 26% of Ghana's peak demand). And the budget could easily hit US$47.2bn. For less frontier use, we can halve these numbers.

30. Counted in the 64-bit arithmetic that scientific supercomputers are ranked by, Ghana's 2027 target is 455 times the world's fastest machine, China's LineShine at 2.2 exaflops, and 53 times all 500 machines on the list combined.

31. Anyone with the barest exposure to Ghana's fiscal context can tell the Minister for free that this won't happen next year. 

32. Ghana's 2035 target of 10²⁵ is 160 times the entire global stock of AI compute today. Even if chips grow 1.4 times more energy-efficient every year, it would draw about 377 GW, 65 times Ghana's current installed generating capacity.

33. I will be charitable and propose that the strategy's drafters may have been thinking about training FLOP (note: without the "per second" at the end). For example, GPT-4's training run used about 2.1×10²⁵ FLOP, the same order of magnitude as Ghana's 2035 endpoint.

34. Unfortunately, that doesn't save the strategy. Recast this way, the target collapses the other way. 10²¹ FLOP is about 12 days' work for one H100 chip at 16-bit precision. 10²⁵ FLOP is one GPT-4-sized training run, which the US$250 million centre could finish in about four months. On that reading the centre meets the 2035 target before its first anniversary. Not meaningful.

35. Given how confusing the overall strategic plan is, would you bank on the first AI compute center and GhanaChat product already being procured at about $270 million? 

36. Here are some bare numbers: the budget, per our modelling, maps to about 2,100 GPUs and 4.3 MW of IT load. That alone adds the equivalent of 90% of Ghana's entire commercial data-centre load in 2024 (4.8 MW). Running it costs about US$76 million a year, which is about six times the revenue of the whole commercial industry.

37. A utilised GPU-hour costs about US$22 at base-case demand, against a market rate of US$6.71 today and roughly US$4.50 averaged over the hardware's life. The base case thus implies a subsidy of about US$61 million a year. 

38. If the concern is about Ministers and their Directors uploading sensitive documents into Gemini or Kimi, then why not a simpler sovereign AI assistant for the civil service first? 

39. That would need roughly 144 GPUs: about 7×10¹⁷ operations a second at 8-bit, US$13 million up front and US$6.7 million a year. That is under a thousandth of the 2027 target, and a far more realistic initial-term strategy. Does Ghana really need to train its base model when orchestrators now allow one to host their own data and switch across multiple advanced open-weight models to serve an Assistant or Agentic system?

40. Howzat?
